{"description":"A consumer reading a tool's served text can predict the tool's behaviour, its reply shape, and what a zero or empty result means, before spending a call on it. The method is the test: predict from the description blind, then call, and score the prediction.

MEASURED 2026-09-11 by that method: 13 of 37 blind-scored read-only tools came back MISS or PARTIAL.

CLOSED SINCE, by merged PRs #477 and #478 — hierarchy_issues, dimension_drift, dimension_drifts, surprising_connections, propose_allocation, alternatives_for, recall_resolutions, mirrors, describe_designs, reconcile_dependencies and reviewed_gaps. One of the thirteen (sync_status) was never a defect: the prediction was wrong, not the tool.

STILL OPEN, and two of them are larger than the original list: compose_and_analyse returns an empty seam set on a purpose-built seam; evidence_report and confirmation_ledger carry undocumented fields; 26 descriptions sit under 220 characters (the bimodal tail); and 76 of 230 required parameters across 68 tools publish NO description at all — surfaced only because the new missing-argument refusal quotes the schema and found nothing to quote. About 21 of those are a constructor's own id and arguably self-evident; roughly 55 are not.

THE CLASS DISCIPLINE THAT APPLIES: where a finding belongs to a class, it is fixed at the class with one contract test that fails on a new member, not one tool at a time.","name":"A tool's served description lets a caller predict what it returns before calling it, including what an empty answer means","provenance":"authored","status":"in_progress","tier":"operational"}
